memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh replied to the heads of the clans of Israel: "The Mighty One, God, the Lord! The Mighty One, God, the Lord! He knows! And let Israel know! If this has been in rebellion or disobedience to the Lord, do not spare us this day. If we have built our own altar to turn away from the Lord and to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, or to sacrifice fellowship offerings on it, may the Lord himself call us to account." — Josh 22:20-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the truth comes out, and it is the opposite of what was feared. The eastern tribes cry out with holy passion: "The Mighty One, God, the Lord! He knows!" They call God Himself as their witness. Far from rebelling, they insist that if this altar was built to turn from God, they would deserve His judgment.

There is deep beauty in their appeal. They rest their innocence not on clever words but on the God who sees the heart. "He knows!" They were content to let the Lord, who searches every motive, be the judge of their intentions.

This is a place we can all stand when we are wrongly accused. We cannot always control what others think of us, but we can appeal to the God who sees perfectly. He knows the truth when no one else does. The Lord weighs the heart (Prov 21:2), and nothing is hidden from Him (Heb 4:13).

Notice their humility too. They did not lash back in anger at being suspected. They earnestly explained themselves and even invited judgment if they were guilty. When you are misunderstood, you can follow their example: answer honestly, appeal to the God who knows your heart, and trust Him to vindicate the truth in His time. He sees what others cannot.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When wrongly accused, do you rest in the God who knows your heart?
2. Can you respond to suspicion with honesty rather than anger?
3. How does it comfort you that God sees the truth about you perfectly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know my heart when others do not. Help me to answer accusations with honesty and humility, and to trust You to defend the truth. Amen.
